prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a rear-end collision claim. Injury: wrist fracture. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1095; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened following a rear-end collision at a signalized intersection. Insured vehicle was stopped at a red light when struck from behind by the third-party vehicle. Claimant reports neck stiffness at the scene and was transported to the emergency department by ambulance. Police report requested. Liability appears clear on the initial account; third-party driver has been contacted and acknowledged the impact.

Entry 2: Claimant called to report a wrist fracture diagnosed at the hospital. Cast applied, follow-up with an orthopedic clinic scheduled. Claimant is not represented by an attorney and says they are handling the matter directly. Explained the claims process and the general steps for injury documentation. Requested medical records authorization form, which claimant agreed to sign and return.

Entry 3: Received the signed medical authorization. Requested records from the emergency department and the orthopedic clinic. Photos of the insured vehicle's rear damage and the claimant's vehicle front damage uploaded to the file. Repair estimate for the claimant's vehicle obtained from the preferred shop. Reviewed the police report, which notes the third-party driver was following too closely.

Entry 4: Spoke with claimant about their work situation. Claimant works in a role requiring repetitive hand use and has been advised by the physician to limit activity for several weeks. Requested wage documentation from the claimant's employer. Claimant has not yet provided a bill summary from the hospital; reminded them that itemized statements will be needed to evaluate the injury claim.

Entry 5: Reviewed incoming records. Emergency department notes confirm the wrist fracture, and the orthopedic follow-up indicates the claimant may require physical therapy. Sent claimant a written summary of documentation still needed, including wage records and itemized bills. Noted that claimant is unrepresented and that all communications have been kept factual and in writing. Diary set for review once records are received.
